question: After the atomic cache repair and exact-head proof are in place, should this PR land the direct Computer Use MCP probe exception, fail-closed readiness defaults, periodic repair, lease surface, and seven new config knobs together?
rationale: The branch changes a sandbox-adjacent app-server boundary, host process cleanup, setup defaults, and public plugin config surface, so code correctness alone cannot decide the permanent product and security contract.

options.title: Harden, Prove, Then Owner-Accept
options.body: Require atomic cache replacement and current-head stale-cache proof, then let Codex/runtime owners explicitly accept the combined boundary and default changes.

options.title: Split The Branch
options.body: Separate cache reconciliation, live readiness, process repair, lease management, docs, and config defaults into smaller owner-reviewed PRs.

options.title: Accept The Broad Contract As-Is
options.body: Maintain the current scope and accept the compatibility, security-boundary, and availability risks once proof is refreshed.

recommendation.title: Harden, Prove, Then Owner-Accept
recommendation.body: Require atomic cache replacement and current-head stale-cache proof, then let Codex/runtime owners explicitly accept the combined boundary and default changes.

likelyOwner.reason: kevinslin has recent merged ownership signals across Codex plugin config, remote app-server plugins, and Computer Use elicitation behavior, which are closest to the product/default choice here.
